description:
Found by the JMAP-g7wu.2.4.6 do-beads triage 2026-05-13.

## Problem

The reference `MemoryBackend::next_id` (and its siblings across all 7 extension-server MemoryBackends) returns simple sequential strings like `"role1"`, `"chat3"`, `"member5"`. draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 references ULIDs as the preferred id form in several places. JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3's acceptance criterion 5 said 'AddRole id is a valid ULID' — but the impl as shipped does not mint ULIDs. A test asserting ULID-format would fail.

This is not a security gap, not a soundness issue, and not a wire-format violation — JMAP-types' Id is a String-shaped opaque token by spec. It's a design-question about whether the reference MemoryBackends should match the spec's apparent preference.

## Open question (human decision required)

Three coherent paths:

### Path A — Keep sequential ids
- Pro: simpler, easier to read in test failures, no new dep (ULID crate)
- Pro: the MemoryBackend is explicitly demo-only per workspace AGENTS.md; production backends are expected to do their own id minting anyway
- Pro: zero migration work — current state is stable
- Con: future contributors comparing reference impl to spec see a divergence

### Path B — Migrate next_id to actual ULIDs across all 7 MemoryBackends
- Pro: matches the spec's apparent preference
- Pro: more realistic for contributors reading the reference impl to learn how a real backend should look
- Con: requires touching all 7 MemoryBackends in one sweep (or filing 7 follow-up beads)
- Con: ULID crate dep across 7 *-server crates (or behind a feature)
- Con: ULIDs sort lexicographically by creation time, which would make some test fixtures less deterministic (or require seeding the ULID generator from a known clock)
- Con: ~3-5 hours of mechanical work for zero functional improvement

### Path C — Make next_id pluggable
- Pro: lets tests pick deterministic ids while production picks ULIDs
- Pro: doesn't lock in either path
- Con: extra trait surface, mostly for a demo-grade impl
- Con: violates the workspace 'MemoryBackend is intentionally demo-quality' posture

## Recommendation

Path A (keep sequential). Rationale: the MemoryBackend exists to support workspace tests and as a contributor reference; it is NOT a model production backend. Asking demo code to mint ULIDs is gold-plating. The spec's ULID preference applies to production backends, which are out of scope for this workspace.

If Path A is chosen, the second action item is to soften the spec's ULID language to 'SHOULD' if it is currently 'MUST', OR file a workspace AGENTS.md note clarifying that reference MemoryBackends are exempt from the ULID preference. (Verify spec wording before filing.)

## Acceptance (path-dependent)

- Decision recorded in this bead's comments.
- If Path A: bead closes with the decision noted; no code change. Optional follow-up: spec-language softening if needed.
- If Path B: 7 sub-beads or one sweep landed; ULID crate dep added; all MemoryBackend tests updated for the new id format.
- If Path C: trait refactor designed and reviewed; one new bead per MemoryBackend implementation.

## Cross-references

- JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3 — the bead whose acceptance criterion 5 surfaced this divergence
- JMAP-g7wu.2.4.6 — the test-matrix bead that triaged this finding
- workspace AGENTS.md — the 'reference MemoryBackend is demo-only' posture this decision depends on
title: MemoryBackend::next_id: design decision on sequential ids vs ULIDs (workspace-wide)
